correctness.rationale: The first-exit Laplace boundary-value problem and reflection-symmetric beta integration yield the exact renewal mean without external lemmas. A positive-integral Watson expansion proves the endpoint-exponent trichotomy; an elementary strict hyperbolic inequality settles the critical alpha=1 infimum. Exact first and second exit-time moments give the small-rate derivative and an interior-minimum existence interval. A uniform differentiable asymptotic expansion, convergence of every minimizer to infinity, and its stationarity prove the 4/epsilon^2 scale and logarithmic optimal-value coefficient. Positivity, alpha>-1, dimensions, r=0 and infinity, and nonuniqueness limitations are explicit. The independent finite 103-assertion verification replay passed; it is not proof of the global theorem.

value.rationale: The presence or absence of a fastest finite restart clock is central to the physical search protocol and is controlled by how strongly the reset-position density suppresses landings near the target. The result establishes a mathematically sharp transition at linear endpoint depletion, a nontrivial finite-optimum regime just above it, and a singular universal 4/(alpha-1)^2 optimal frequency with a logarithmic optimal-value expansion. Neither a fixed-rate hypergeometric substitution nor an isolated numerical optimum answers this combined design question.
